audit: (1) Recurrent identical variants spread across unrelated diagnoses (C17orf80 p.S281R in 72 cases, HLTF p.Q898E 44, ZNF510 p.Q248E 32, CD69 p.L176Q 23, CD46 p.K388N 22, SLAMF7, TSPAN19, CCDC168 p.Q1530*, etc.) look like germline polymorphisms or pipeline artifacts; I removed them before testing. (2) About 15 hypermutated tumors (500 to 15,700 calls, mostly 'Glioma, malignant' and 'Neoplasm, malignant') inflate large-gene hits (TTN, MUC16, OBSCN); I excluded cases with more than 500 calls from the association tests. (3) Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and partly uninformative ('missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm, malignant', 'Neoplasm, uncertain whether benign or malignant', 'Glioma, malignant' as a catch-all for HGG/DIPG), overlapping subtypes are tested as separate labels (medulloblastoma NOS vs desmoplastic/large cell; RMS NOS vs embryonal/alveolar), and many diagnoses have fewer than 10 cases, so frequencies are imprecise. (4) Four strong signals are not known biology and have an unusual pattern: PIK3R1 in pilocytic astrocytoma (30/168, spread evenly along the protein rather than in the iSH2 hotspot where PIK3R1 indels cluster in glioma), ARID1B in RMS NOS (16/66, all missense, every position unique), ZMYM3 in 'Glioma, malignant' and ASXL1 in medulloblastoma (missense spread across the protein, not the truncating pattern expected for these genes). They might be real new findings, but they could also be artifacts or contamination from how the data were processed. I report them with reduced probability and they need orthogonal validation. (5) There is no batch, center or sequencing-platform field, so I could not check for batch confounding. Fusions and copy-number changes (e.g. KIAA1549-BRAF in pilocytic astrocytoma) are absent, so frequencies understate driver prevalence. Protein numbering follows a non-canonical transcript in places (BRAF V640E = V600E, H3-3A K28M = K27M).
methods: Built a case-by-gene binary matrix of non-synonymous mutations after removing artifact-like recurrent variants (the same protein change in 8 or more cases across 6 or more diagnoses, outside known driver genes) and excluding hypermutated tumors (more than 500 calls) from testing. For every diagnosis label with 2 or more mutated cases and every gene mutated in 3 or more cases, I ran a one-sided Fisher exact test of that diagnosis against all other cases and applied Benjamini-Hochberg correction. I then checked the significant hits for hotspot recurrence, variant-class mix, protein-position distribution, co-mutation and mutation burden, and set probabilities from the strength of the statistics plus prior biological knowledge. Expected frequency is (mutated cases + 0.5)/(cases with that diagnosis + 1).
